title: Vietnam draft lottery as IV for military service on earnings

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
I will use Instrumental Variables (IV) estimation with draft lottery number as an instrument for veteran status. The key assumptions are: (1) **Relevance**: Low lottery numbers increase probability of military service, (2) **Exclusion restriction**: Lottery numbers only affect earnings through military service (random assignment ensures this), and (3) **Monotonicity**: Lower numbers don't decrease service probability for anyone. The draft lottery's randomness provides exogenous variation in military service, addressing selection bias from voluntary enlistment.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(stargazer)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s21_data.csv")

# Examine the data structure
print("Data summary:")
print(summary(data))
print(paste("Sample size:", nrow(data)))

# Create binary instrument: drafted (lottery number <= 195, approximate cutoff)
# In reality, lower numbers had higher draft probability
data$drafted <- as.numeric(data$z <= 195)

# Check instrument strength (first stage)
print("\n=== FIRST STAGE REGRESSION ===")
first_stage <- lm(x ~ drafted + controls, data = data)
print(summary(first_stage))

# F-statistic for instrument strength
f_stat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1]
print(paste("First-stage F-statistic:", round(f_stat, 3)))

# Check if F > 10 (rule of thumb for strong instrument)
print(paste("Strong instrument (F > 10):", f_stat > 10))

# Reduced form (direct effect of instrument on outcome)
print("\n=== REDUCED FORM REGRESSION ===")
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ drafted + controls, data = data)
print(summary(reduced_form))

# Main IV estimation using 2SLS
print("\n=== IV ESTIMATION (2SLS) ===")
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | drafted + controls, data = data)
print(summary(iv_model))

# Extract key coefficient
iv_coeff <- coef(iv_model)["x"]
iv_se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(iv_model)))["x"]
print(paste("\nMain IV Result:"))
print(paste("Coefficient on veteran status:", round(iv_coeff, 4)))
print(paste("Standard error:", round(iv_se, 4)))
print(paste("95% CI: [", round(iv_coeff - 1.96*iv_se, 4), ", ", 
            round(iv_coeff + 1.96*iv_se, 4), "]"))

# OLS for comparison (biased due to selection)
print("\n=== OLS COMPARISON (likely biased) ===")
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
ols_coeff <- coef(ols_model)["x"]
print(paste("OLS coefficient:", round(ols_coeff, 4)))
print(paste("IV vs OLS difference:", round(iv_coeff - ols_coeff, 4)))

# Robustness checks
print("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===")

# 1. Alternative cutoff points
cutoffs <- c(150, 175, 200, 225)
iv_results <- sapply(cutoffs, function(cut) {
  data$drafted_alt <- as.numeric(data$z <= cut)
  iv_alt <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | drafted_alt + controls, data = data)
  coef(iv_alt)["x"]
})
print("IV estimates with different cutoffs:")
print(data.frame(Cutoff = cutoffs, IV_Coeff = round(iv_results, 4)))

# 2. Continuous instrument (lottery number directly)
print("\nUsing continuous lottery number as instrument:")
iv_continuous <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
print(paste("Continuous IV coefficient:", round(coef(iv_continuous)["x"], 4)))

# Final result
print(paste("\n=== FINAL RESULT ==="))
print(paste("Effect of military service on log earnings:", round(iv_coeff, 4)))
if(iv_coeff < 0) {
  print(paste("Military service reduces earnings by approximately", 
              round(abs(iv_coeff)*100, 1), "percent"))
} else {
  print(paste("Military service increases earnings by approximately", 
              round(iv_coeff*100, 1), "percent"))
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a **negative coefficient** of approximately **-0.15 to -0.25**, indicating that military service reduces long-run civilian earnings by 15-25%. This reflects the opportunity cost of time spent in military rather than accumulating civilian work experience, human capital, or education. The IV estimate should be more negative than OLS because OLS suffers from positive selection bias (men who voluntarily enlist may have unobserved characteristics that increase earnings). The draft lottery provides credible exogenous variation to identify the causal effect of military service on earnings.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV/2SLS — instrument: draft lottery number; LATE for compliers (drafted but wouldn't have volunteered)
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Military service reduces earnings for complier veterans
